answer.answer: The study confirmed 4 of the 5 cases it was asked for, so the goal was not met. The 4 cases are 18f8dbd6 at 1.4x / −1 s (S18), 07981e6a at 1.4x / −1 s (S3), 0e002edd at 1.4x / −1 s (S11) and 1bbe02fc at 1.2x / −1 s (S20). None of the triaged failures involved the pedestrian. The policy hit other cars or parked cars after drifting left or not braking for a slow lead car, or it was flagged offroad. What drives the failures is high hand-off speed, often with a RIGHT route command the policy did not follow, not the pedestrian's timing. The 1bbe02fc case may say more about the map than the policy: its offroad flags are marginal (under 1 m off the human path), it also failed in its single run at 1.0x (a hint, not a rate), and every S11 failure is marked as a possible simulator artifact, although triage blames the policy in each.

findings.claim: On 18f8dbd6 at 1.4x / −1 s, every run failed the same way: at about 12 m/s the policy steered left into the next lane and hit vehicle 2, while the recorded route bore right. At 1.2x / −0.5 s, its single run did not fail.

On 07981e6a at 1.4x / −1 s, every run failed. The ego drifted left on a narrow residential street and clipped parked car 6 without braking enough. That is a policy failure with no pedestrian involved.

On 0e002edd, every run at 1.4x / −1 s failed: the ego crept into the intersection and hit crossing car 112, or swung left into a parked car. Every one of these failures is marked as a possible artifact (ego over 3.5 m from the recorded trajectory), but triage puts the policy at fault each time. Single runs at 0.8x to 1.2x with shifts of −1 s to +0.5 s did not fail.

On 1bbe02fc, every run at 1.2x / −1 s was flagged as leaving the road at the stop line, where the route turns right. In each run the ego was under 1 m from the human path, and triage could not say whether the policy was at fault. The single run at 1.0x / −1 s failed the same way, so this scene may fail without any speed increase and the flag may be a drivable-area boundary quirk.

The best candidates for a fifth case are not confirmed: 18d28973 at 1.4x / −1.5 s and 0d4893f5 at 1.4x / −1 s. In both, the failure ranges reach below 0.5 even after many repeats. 18d28973 failures were rear-end hits on slowing car 99 after the policy ignored a RIGHT command. 0d4893f5 failures were left-drift sideswipes of car 33.

On 18d28973 at 1.4x, the shifts of −1.5 s and −2 s produced failures and −1 s produced none in its few runs. Triage shows the collisions were with car 99, not the pedestrian, so this timing effect is a hint at most.
No setting failed on 048b974e, 0b10bce8 or 12a09194, including 1.4x on 048b974e and 12a09194, but each of those settings had only one or two runs.

open: No scene was run at the nominal 1.0x / 0 s, so the study cannot show that the confirmed failures need the speed–timing change rather than happening anyway. Repeats at 1.0x / 0 s on 18f8dbd6, 07981e6a, 0e002edd and 1bbe02fc would settle this.

The pedestrian's timing has no shown effect, and no failure involved the pedestrian. Almost all runs used shifts of −2 s to −0.5 s at 1.2x to 1.4x. Ego speeds of 0.6x to 0.8x and positive shifts were barely or never tried, so pedestrian-strike cases were not searched. Sweeping the shift from −2 s to +2 s at a fixed 1.4x on one confirmed scene would show whether timing matters.
Fifth case: more repeats at 18d28973 1.4x / −1.5 s or 0d4893f5 1.4x / −1 s could narrow the ranges. Both currently sit around 0.5, so they may not be confirmed even then.
Whether the 1bbe02fc offroad flags are real departures or map drivable-area artifacts. Checking the map boundary at that stop line, plus more runs at 1.0x, would settle it.
Whether the S11 failures, all flagged as possible artifacts, are reproducible after a rendering check.
The comparison with the 10 Hz study pedestrian_ego_speed needs that study's results next to these. This report does not include them.
